follow-up time: N/A - study period from January 1, 2014 to December 31, 2020
cohort: 298 pairs of women from California, Florida, and a northeastern state (USA) matched on age, race/ethnicity, state, socioeconomic status, and hospital type
finding: The use of doulas appears an effective strategy for improving maternal health, especially among socioeconomically vulnerable and marginalized minority populations.
mod_finding: Women who received doula care had 52.9% lower odds of cesarean delivery (OR: 0.471 95% CI: 0.29-0.79).
